source_row.rationale: Malingering involves the intentional production of symptoms motivated by an identifiable external incentive (such as financial compensation, avoiding work/legal responsibility, or obtaining medications), distinguishing it from factitious disorder, in which the motivation is understood to be primarily psychological rather than tied to external gain. Malingering itself is not classified as a mental disorder in the DSM-5-TR, but rather as a condition that may be a focus of clinical attention.
source_row.source_detail: DSM-5-TR distinction: deliberate symptom fabrication/exaggeration associated with external incentives; updated 2026; accessed 2026-08-14.
